summary: A two-day marine science program for 90 middle school students in Key Largo, with groups of 30 rotating through reef snorkeling and fish surveys, mangrove kayaking, and a lionfish dissection before a day of coral ecology and citizen science.

days.title: Welcome to the Reef
days.theme: Three groups of 30 rotate through reef snorkeling, mangrove kayaking, and a lionfish lesson.

blocks.title: Arrival & Welcome
blocks.description: Your group arrives in Key Largo. REEF educators welcome the group, preview the day, and introduce the three groups of 30 students.

blocks.title: Rotation 1: Reef, Mangroves & Lionfish
blocks.description: Each group of 30 students takes part in one of three stations: reef snorkel and fish surveys, mangrove kayaking, or a lionfish lesson and dissection. Over three rotations, every group visits all three stations. Station order is confirmed once boat times are set.

blocks.title: Lunch (on your own)
blocks.description: Lunch is not included in this proposal. Your group can bring lunch or pick up food nearby.

blocks.title: Rotation 2: Reef, Mangroves & Lionfish
blocks.description: Each group of 30 students takes part in one of three stations: reef snorkel and fish surveys, mangrove kayaking, or a lionfish lesson and dissection. Over three rotations, every group visits all three stations. Station order is confirmed once boat times are set.

blocks.title: Rotation 3: Reef, Mangroves & Lionfish
blocks.description: Each group of 30 students takes part in one of three stations: reef snorkel and fish surveys, mangrove kayaking, or a lionfish lesson and dissection. Over three rotations, every group visits all three stations. Station order is confirmed once boat times are set.

studentsWill: Snorkel a Key Largo coral reef and record the fish they find.
Explore a mangrove ecosystem by kayak.
Investigate invasive lionfish through a guided dissection.

days.title: Coral, Fish & Citizen Science
days.theme: Study how a coral reef works, sharpen your fish ID skills, and learn how citizen scientists contribute real data.

blocks.title: Coral Reef Ecology
blocks.description: A Florida Keys coral lesson on how reefs are built, how the organisms on them depend on each other, and how coral restoration helps reefs recover.

blocks.title: Fish ID & Seine Netting
blocks.description: Students build fish identification skills and use seine netting to sample and identify fish up close.

blocks.title: Lunch (on your own)
blocks.description: Lunch is not included in this proposal. Your group can bring lunch or pick up food nearby.

blocks.title: Citizen Science & the Volunteer Fish Survey Project
blocks.description: Students learn how REEF's volunteer divers and snorkelers record the fish they see, and why that data matters to scientists and reef managers. They practice the survey method they will use on the reef.

blocks.title: Departure
blocks.description: Your group departs. Lunch is not included in this proposal.

studentsWill: Explain how coral reefs function as connected ecosystems.
Practice fish identification and sample fish with seine nets.
Understand how REEF fish survey data is collected and used.
